newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends sharply lower on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends sharply lower on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures ended sharply lower Friday in a sluggish session, with spot-February leading the way amid forecasts for much milder weather next week, industry sources said.
February tumbled 40 cents to close at $2.984 per million British thermal units. March settled 32 cents lower at $2.68. Other deferreds ended down by 1.2 to 15 cents.

"I see more downside risk for the next week or so because the (cold) weather is not there," said one Texas-based trader, noting weaker technicals also were likely to pressure the complex, particularly with February's close today below $3.00.
With 6-10 day forecasts calling for well-above normal temperatures for most of the nation, many now expected cash and futures to stay on the defensive near-term.
But some expected a rebound despite bearish weather patterns, noting February was significantly oversold after a 24 percent dive in four sessions and the bulk of winter was still ahead.

Chart traders said a double top and an island reversal on the perpetual chart this week helped trigger the two-day flood of long liquidation and technical selling. They said Feb's close below psychological support at $3.00 could mean a move to the $2.77 area, a prominent low from December 3. Resistance was still seen at Thursday's $3.595-3.61 gap and at the contract high of $4.02.

In the cash, December Gulf prices tumbled 40 cents Friday to the $3.10 level, with January hard to peg but notionally quoted in the $3.20s, down about 45 cents. December Midcontinent gas was talked 60-70 cents lower in the $2.90 area. December New York city gate gas sold between $3.45 and $3.70, down 25-50 cents on the day.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip skidded another 13.6 cents to $2.285. NYMEX said 23,849 contracts traded, up from Thursday's revised tally of 19,849.
NYMEX January Alberta natgas expired four cents higher at $1.72, while deferred months were untraded. NYMEX said three Alberta contracts changed hands.
NYMEX Permian natgas did not trade, but January settled five cents lower at $4.00.

On the KCBT, February closed down 39 cents at $2.79. Most deferred months were untraded. The East/West spread narrowed by one cent to 19.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 85 lots traded, down from Thursday's 534.
